newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT- Gold faces test of lows despite gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Gold faces test of lows despite gains.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold has resurfaced above the key $340 area on Wednesday but analysts are not convinced about the early gains and forecast an ominous test of $336.15 support.
Silver was also likely to gravitate towards the technical level of $4.45 with little buying interest around, while platinum could continue to buck the trend with no word on delayed Russian supplies.
GOLD - Bullion popped up above $340 after falling from that key level on Monday as options-related support faded.
But analysts saw little room for gains, with fundamentals still affected by the prospect of central bank sales.
"The attitude (of central banks) towards gold has changed. That's why I don't see any fundamental reason to buy gold," said precious metals analyst Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corporation.

Gold was poised to test the February 12 low of $336.15 in the near term, but support was quite fragile and so further losses to the next technical level of $325 -- a four-year low -- could be expected.
Gold's prospects took a further blow on Tuesday after a report that the Swiss would drop their opposition to the IMF selling its gold reserves to fund a debt relief programme to poor countries.
The market saw early buying interest from the Middle East, although professional dealers continued to shun gold, traders said.
Some support also came from a drifting dollar after weak U.S. economic data on Tuesday suggested interest rates might not be increased after all.
Attention will focus on U.S. GDP data for the first quarter on Wednesday for fresh clues.
Analysts said gold would need to break above the key $345 level to strengthen its technical picture. But a downtrend line from the highs above $363 capped the upside at around $341.
By 0800 GMT spot gold was indicated at $340.50/340.80 an ounce compared with New York's close of $339.70/$340.20.
SILVER - Silver had also emerged from its lows on Wednesday in tandem with gold, but a dive to $4.45 was not ruled out by technical analysts.
Silver's outlook turned negative after bears raided the key support of $4.65 after the expiry of OTC options on Monday, pushing the market to $4.59.
At 0800 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.67/$4.69 an ounce from its New York close of $4.65/$4.67.
"It's up with gold but we could see some downward pressure," said Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corporation.
A weaker dollar after fears of U.S. interest rate rise were dimmed could help the precious metals, but any impact was likely to be short-term, he added.
PLATINUM - The metal forged ahead on Wednesday, stepping closer to $375 resistance after falls earlier this week.
Hausheer said platinum was likely to remain in a roller-coaster range, but further delays in Russian shipments would push the market higher.
Technical support was pegged strongly at $370.
By 0915 GMT platinum was quoted at $374.00/$375.00 an ounce from New York's close of $373.30/$374.30.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
